licton_springs_tudor_restoration.heading: Tudor Exterior Restoration and Bathroom/Laundry Renovation in Licton Springs
licton_springs_tudor_restoration.text1: This Licton Springs project restored a distinctive Tudor home while also improving its bathroom and laundry spaces. Because this old-world architecture is unusual in Seattle, the curved rooflines, brickwork, stucco, and trim were especially important to preserve.
licton_springs_tudor_restoration.text2: The exterior work included cleaning and re-tuckpointing the brick, replacing deteriorated mortar, removing rotten wood, rebuilding straight and curved trim, repairing stucco in the gables and rounded entry, and renewing the laundry-room entrance with a new door.
licton_springs_tudor_restoration.text3: Alongside the exterior restoration, the project scope also included bathroom and laundry improvements to support better everyday use. Together, the work paired practical interior updates with a careful exterior restoration that made the whole property feel more complete.
licton_springs_tudor_restoration.short2: Tudor Exterior Restoration and Bathroom/Laundry Renovation in Licton Springs
licton_springs_tudor_restoration.text4: Explore how masonry repair, stucco, trim, entries, and interior utility spaces were coordinated to restore the home as one complete property.

part1.small_heading: A rare Tudor home with a unique architectural identity
part1.text2: This Tudor home reflects a Northern European architectural style that feels uncommon in Seattle. The steep gables, brick walls, and distinctive trim made the home stand out right away, which is why the remodel needed to preserve the character instead of flattening it into a generic exterior update.

part2.small_heading: Brick cleaning and re-tuck-pointing throughout the exterior
part2.text2: A major part of the project was restoring the brick envelope. The mortar was badly aged and, in some areas, the bricks were close to failing, so the masonry had to be cleaned and the joints carefully rebuilt.
part2.text3: Re-tuck-pointing the brick gave the walls structural stability again while also sharpening the look of the exterior. The same restoration continued around the chimney and side walls, not just the front facade.

part3.small_heading: Gables, stucco, and detailed trim rebuilt with care
part3.text2: The gables and upper wall sections also needed significant attention. Rotten wood was removed, trim pieces were rebuilt, and the stucco was redone so the Tudor detailing would feel crisp again instead of tired or patched together.
part3.text3: The rounded and angled wood details required especially careful custom cuts.

part4.small_heading: Entry improvements and a rebuilt laundry-room door
part4.text2: The remodel also included work at the laundry-room entry. This door area was rebuilt and fitted with a new door, improving both function and the finished appearance of the service-side access point.
